newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Gas Board profit up 22 pct at 82 mln punts.
newsitem.headline: Irish Gas Board profit up 22 pct at 82 mln punts.

text.p: Ireland's state-owned gas board, Bord Gais, reported a rise of 22 percent in 1996 pre-tax profits to 82 million punts on turnover of 271 million punts, it said on Wednesday.
The company said its strong performance was due to a 13 percent increase in overall sales of natural gas, with the residential sector being particularly buoyant, increasing by 20 percent on 1995.
"By Irish standards, 1996 was a cold year in weather terms and this was reflected in the volume of natural gas consumed during the year," Bord Gais said in a results statement.
Operating costs in 1996 were seven percent higher than in 1995, due mostly to rationalisation provisions, it said.
Depreciation was 15 percent higher while interest payable was 19 percent lower than in 1995.
The gas board said it invested capital expenditure of 43 million punts, which was sourced from internal resources, on the development of the natural gas network.
It said company borrowings in 1996 were reduced by 58 million punts in 1996 to 149 million.
